Incorrect premise: incremental update only ever processes brand-new SKUs (postgres_skus - sqlite_skus), never re-touches existing ones, so there's nothing unchanged to skip there. --force/--all is intentionally a from-scratch rebuild, so checksum-skipping would undermine its purpose. No real benefit.

Measured with real instrumentation added for this issue (per-stage timing in generate_and_store_embeddings). Two full 4269-product reindex runs post-DirectML-fix: ETL ~2m38-39s, embed-loop ~26-27.5s total with sqlite_read=0.0s (0%), embed=23-24.5s (89%), chroma_upsert=2.9-3.0s (11%). SQLite read time is negligible/unmeasurable, so there is no meaningful I/O to overlap with compute — embed-loop is compute-bound on ONNX/DirectML inference, not I/O-bound. Producer/consumer prefetch would add complexity for no measurable gain. Not pursuing.
